Christian Mensah knows, by scenario 5, that Jonathan was being framed and that the real culprit is someone close to both of them. He also knows enough to say he has “found out who is behind this,” and he tells Jonathan that he is going to confront that person and bring them to justice.

However, scenario 5 does not say the confrontation has already happened. It says Christian “decides to confront” the real culprit and says, “I’m going to confront them.” That is an intention or planned action, not a completed action.

Thus:
- It is not merely that Christian feels betrayed and resolute (b), because that is an emotional state.
- It is not that Christian actually confronts the culprit (c), because the text only states he intends/plans to do so.
- The best match is that Christian intends to confront the real culprit.

ANSWER: h
